extracted.intended_audience: indie and traditionally published authors seeking freelance editorial services; freelance editorial professionals considering EFA membership
extracted.subtask_description: Finding, evaluating, and selecting freelance editorial professionals (developmental editors, copyeditors, proofreaders, sensitivity readers, book coaches, etc.) for manuscripts, books, and related publishing projects. Also describes the kinds of editorial services and standards freelance editors provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help your characters come alive
rubrics_metrics.description: Help your characters come alive for readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an editor I will use my abilities to help you write full, engaging characters that readers love, or love to hate! (Katy Grenfell — offered as a core developmental objective.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft a compelling story
rubrics_metrics.description: Help you craft a compelling story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors offer guidance on crafting story from first draft to final performance and will help you tell the most engaging version of your story (Katy Grenfell). Implies attention to plot, pacing, conflict, and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Push the writer beyond comfort zones
rubrics_metrics.description: Nudge the author’s imagination beyond their comfort zone to reach new places in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may deliberately push writers to explore riskier or less familiar creative choices to strengthen the work (Katy Grenfell: 'Help you work outside your comfort zone').

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal-oriented coaching and craft development
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with the author as a coach to help them meet and surpass their writing goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers support, honest feedback, and a partnership approach to develop craft and achieve authorial objectives (Katy Grenfell: 'Help you achieve your goals as a writer'; Cody Sisco: 'partner with you to improve the written product and to develop your craft').

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental editing (fiction and scripts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Developmental/substantive editing of fiction, scripts, screenplays, and long-form narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services explicitly listed: Developmental Editing for Fiction (Sci‑Fi/Fantasy, Adventure/Suspense, Mystery, Historical Fiction, Horror, YA, Comedy, True Crime, etc.), scripts, screenplays, and book coaching. Includes structural, character, pacing, and big-picture story work (multiple bios).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity reading and authenticity review
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity reading for representation and avoidance of harmful or inaccurate portrayals (e.g., fat/obese/BBW, female sexuality, sexual assault/trauma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers targeted sensitivity reading to ensure authentic, responsible representation and to avoid problematic wording; may focus on specific identity/experience areas listed by the editor (Katy Grenfell, Ellis Harvey‑Prybylski, Dayna Reidenouer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Book coaching and beta reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Book coaching and beta reading to support drafting, revision strategy, and early-reader feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services include ongoing coaching (weekly sessions), beta reading (as time allows), and feedback memos to guide revision and next steps (Dayna Reidenouer, Cyndi Sandusky).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final polish / proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofreading and final polish to eliminate typos, grammar issues, and punctuation errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors offer final-polish proofreading services for a polished finished product; may include meticulous line-level corrections and typographical cleanup (Ronane Lloyd; Dave Pasquantonio).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bigger-picture commentary / manuscript assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide commentary on bigger-picture issues such as structure, story flow, and overarching problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include thorough feedback memos covering many areas (Dayna Reidenouer: 'thorough feedback memo that covered 14 different areas, including structure') and editors noting where macro-level changes are needed (Ronane Lloyd: 'commentary on bigger-picture issues').

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyediting, line editing, revision/rewriting, ghostwriting
rubrics_metrics.description: Mid- and micro-level editorial services: line editing, copyediting, revision/rewriting, and ghostwriting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors explicitly list these service types (Sheryl Holmberg and others); guidance implies selection based on project stage and needs (manuscript polish vs. substantive rework).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking and house-style compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-checking and application of house/style-guide rules (Chicago, AP, custom house styles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors provide fact-checking and are familiar with common style guides (Jean Gazis: 'familiar with Chicago and AP styles'); some offer creation or enforcement of house style guides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre and subject-matter expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor subject-matter and genre expertise (literary, historical fiction, mystery/thriller, memoir, natural history, parenting, business, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors advertise specialties and topical knowledge; selecting an editor with relevant genre/subject expertise is presented as a quality criterion (Jean Gazis, Sheryl Holmberg, Ellis Harvey‑Prybylski, Dayna Reidenouer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity, inclusion, and avoidance of problematic wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep content authentic and inclusive while avoiding problematic or harmful wording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors offer to ensure authenticity and inclusion in manuscripts and to flag or revise problematic language (Ronane Lloyd; EFA DEI statements). Sensitivity readers and equity-focused editors explicitly support this aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability: meeting expectations and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to work to client expectations and to deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors promote reliability as a professional attribute (Ronane Lloyd: 'Ability to work to expectations and to deadline') — an implicit selection/evaluation criterion for freelance editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample edit to assess fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer a paid or complimentary sample edit of a short excerpt (e.g., 1,000–1,500 words) so client and editor can test fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some editors offer sample edits to determine compatibility and editorial approach before committing to a full project (Cyndi Sandusky: 'I am happy to do a sample edit of 1000‑1500 words so we can see if we’re a good fit').

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured feedback memos across multiple areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide organized feedback memos that cover multiple aspects of the manuscript (structure, fact‑checking, story flow, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clients report receiving thorough memos that enumerate areas for revision and explain rationale (Dayna Reidenouer testimonial: 'thorough feedback memo that covered 14 different areas, including structure'; includes comments on fact‑checking and story flow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic/substantive editing and dissertation coaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Developmental/substantive content editing and coaching for dissertations, theses, journal articles, and other scholarly products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors with academic backgrounds offer specialized services for scholarly work, advising on methodology, argumentation, and institutional expectations (Sheryl Lieb: dissertation coach and developmental editor for academic clients).

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-publishing and production support (typesetting, e-book formatting, design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance with self-publishing tasks such as typesetting for print, e-book formatting, page layout, and cover/graphic design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors offer production and design services to help authors bring books into print and digital formats (Sheryl Holmberg: 'typesetting (Print), E-Book Formatting, ... create original page layouts, logos and graphic elements').

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized sensitivity foci (disability, LGBTQIA+, neurodivergence, mental illness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity-reading specialties focused on disability, LGBTQIA+, neurodivergence, mental health, and other identity/experience areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several editors list focused sensitivity-reading areas (Ellis Harvey‑Prybylski, Dayna Reidenouer), indicating the value of matching reader lived experience to the material being reviewed for authenticity and harm reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible editorial partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: An editorial approach that is flexible and collaborative, partnering with the author rather than imposing a single fixed style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors describe themselves as collaborative partners who adapt style and tone to the author’s voice and project goals (Cody Sisco: 'My editing style is flexible and my goal is to partner with you').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use EFA member directory and editorial rates chart to select professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Select editors using the EFA Member Directory and consult the annually updated editorial rates chart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EFA provides resources to help clients find qualified professionals and compare rates; these resources imply criteria for selection such as credentials, specialties, and rates (EFA Provides: 'editorial rates chart', 'Member Directory and Job List').
